title: Route every way of asking who needs a reply to the inbox answer
requested_outcome: On 2026-09-24 the owner asked 'any customers who need a reply' twice and once got an answer about orders to go out. On the trunk the fast path sends 'any customers who need a reply' and 'who needs a reply' to the needs_reply family, but 'anyone waiting on a reply' falls below the family's confidence floor and goes to the model, and 'customers who need a reply?' is classed as a mutation ('asks for a change') because 'reply' is read as an instruction to send one. Fix app/fastpath/intent.py (and the family's signals if needed) so that questions about who is waiting on or needs a reply resolve to needs_reply with confidence above the floor, while real instructions ('reply to Mia', 'send a reply to order 2044') still resolve as the compose or reply change they are. Add a table-driven test covering at least: any customers who need a reply; customers who need a reply?; anyone waiting on a reply; who's waiting for a reply; does anyone need an answer from us; any emails I haven't replied to; is anyone waiting on me; and the instruction cases, asserting the family and that no question is classed as a mutation. Run every check listed below in your workspace and fix anything it reports before you report. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically after your candidate is published.
acceptance_criteria: every listed question resolves to needs_reply above the confidence floor and none is classed as a mutation
the instruction cases still resolve as reply or compose changes
existing fastpath and family tests pass unchanged
every listed check passes in the worker's workspace
